I'd be happy to help. Download Linux Mint (It's most like Windows), or Ubuntu. They are the two most popular Linux distributions. There are literally dozens upon dozens, but these two are the most popular. There's also another one called Linux Deepin, which I do like, but isn't popular enough yet for me to recommend them. It's always nice to be running a popular distribution of Linux, so in case you have a question or a problem, chances are you have someone who can help.

First off, BACK UP YOUR FILES. If you are careful, you'll be fine, but it's always a good idea to have a backup of your files.

http://www.linuxmint.com/edition.php?id=190

http://www.ubuntu.com/download/desktop

They will download a large file called an ISO file. Burn that to a cd or usb thumb drive (let me know if you don't know how to do that).

Restart your computer, and depending on which manufacturer you have, you may have to hit F10 or F12 or some other key to bring up what's known as a boot menu. Use your arrow keys to highlight the cd-rom or flash drive option (depending on how you burned the ISO file), and hit enter.

The cd/usb will then boot into a temporary environment, and you can either poke around and play with Linux, or install it. I recommend playing around with it first, making sure your various devices work (video, sound, wireless networking, etc).

Once you're sure everything is good to go, then you'll see an icon on the desktop to install Linux. Double click on it, and follow the prompts when it asks you various questions such as what do you want for a password, what's your time zone, etc. They will ask you if you want to wipe out your Windows install, install Linux side by side with Windows, or something else. Choose the option you want. If you choose side by side, when you boot your computer up, a small window will pop up every time asking you if you want to boot into Windows or Linux.
